text:
Priya Sharma: Hey folks — RateForge sent our renewal (INV-RF-2026) and the line items don't match our usage report. They billed for 10 seats + 200k included API calls/month, but our onboarding invoices show we were on a consumption plan. Can someone take a look?

Evan Cole: Do we have the invoice PDF? I can pull last quarter's usage.

Priya Sharma: Uploaded: https://files.redwood/procurement/rateforge_renewal_april.pdf — summary: Renewal list price $120k/yr (10 seats + 200k/mo), one-time onboarding $7,500, overage $0.008/call.

Evan Cole: Quick math — our usage last 3 months was: Nov 2025 420k, Dec 2025 380k, Jan 2026 410k. That's ~4.9M/year. If included 200k/mo = 2.4M/yr, so ~2.5M calls over. At $0.008 that's ~20k/yr in overages, but seat pricing seems high if we don't need seats for most users.

Priya Sharma: Exactly. We never migrated to their seat-pack; we were using API-first. Looks like sales assumed seat model for renewal. Nora — can you confirm how RateForge computed included volume?

Nora (RateForge Sales): Hi Priya, thanks for flagging. Apologies for the confusion — the renewal template defaulted to our Team bundle. I can switch you to a committed consumption agreement. Options: (A) Committed 5M calls/yr at $0.0055/call + seats $6k/yr = $33,500/yr total, onboarding waived for a pilot. (B) 3M commit at $0.0065/call + seats $4k = $22,500/yr, onboarding waived. Both include monthly reporting and a 30-day evaluation with full refund.

Evan Cole: Option A pricing math: 5M * $0.0055 = $27,500 + $6k seats = $33,500 — that's way lower than the $120k list. Good. Need to confirm: is that locked for 12 months? Any ramp clauses?

Nora (RateForge Sales): Lock for 12 months if signed by end of month. Ramp: if monthly usage exceeds 150% of monthly average commit for two consecutive months, we'll trigger a review and may propose a supplemental addendum. Overage rate after commit is $0.007/call.

Priya Sharma: Procurement checklist for counter: 1) Get committed unit price in writing for 12 months. 2) Explicit monthly dollar cap for overages (not just %). 3) Pilot credit or onboarding waived confirmed in contract language. 4) Termination rights during pilot (45 days). 5) Net30 payment. 6) SOC2 and data processing addendum.

Evan Cole: Also ask for invoice alignment: update the invoice to show "Committed Consumption" line with the math so our AP team can reconcile.

Nora (RateForge Sales): Can do. For the monthly cap — would $3,000/mo cap on overages work? That maps to ~428k extra calls at $0.007/call.

Priya Sharma: $3k/mo sounds reasonable. Ask Legal: include a clause that allows one-time re-negotiation if usage consistently exceeds commit for 3 months.

FinanceBot: Note: Procurement approval required for commits > $25k/yr. Please route to FinanceOps for sign-off. See https://intra.redwood/finance/commit-approval.

Evan Cole: I'm drafting the counter-email. Will include last quarter usage CSV:
```
month,api_calls
2025-11,420000
2025-12,380000
2026-01,410000
```

Priya Sharma: Draft subject suggestion: "RateForge renewal — request for committed consumption pricing & invoice correction (Redwood Inference)". Evan, drop the draft here once ready.

Nora (RateForge Sales): Quick follow: If you sign the 5M commit today, I can add a one-time credit of $5k to offset onboarding. Otherwise 3M commit still gets onboarding waived.

Evan Cole: Copy. We'll prefer the 5M commit if Finance approves. Priya, I'll post the draft in ~20min for review.

Priya Sharma: Thanks team — please make sure AP/Legal see the updated invoice before we sign. Thumbs-up once draft is posted. :thumbsup:
